- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.6), model over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–3% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- Model consistently under-responds to sharp upward sentiment spikes; if sentiment jumps >0.6 in 3–5 days, add 2–5% to forecast horizon.
- Model over-anticipates downward sentiment shifts; if sentiment drops >-0.6 in 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if recent 7-day average is >10% above 30d moving avg, forecast should be capped at 10% below that avg; if below, allow slight overshoot.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true trend by 2–5 days; if sentiment is trending upward, shift forecast 1–3 days ahead; if downward, shift back 1–2 days.
- Overshoot after spikes: if true outcome spikes >10% above recent high, model often over-forecasts by 5–10% in next 5 days; apply 5–10% downward correction.
- Sentiment volatility >0.4 in 3 consecutive days triggers “sentiment shock” correction: adjust forecast ±2–5% based on sentiment direction (up = +, down = -).
